strings.name: Sanjay Mehrotra
strings.role: Semiconductor engineer and Micron chairman and CEO
strings.summary: Mehrotra began in memory-chip design, co-founded SanDisk and later became its president and CEO, leading business expansion. He became Micron CEO in 2017 and chairman in 2025, directing technology, product and manufacturing investment amid memory cycles and changing AI demand.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He co-founded SanDisk and contributed to Micron’s development, advancing the commercialization and large-scale manufacture of flash and memory technology.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: EECS B.S. (1978) and M.S. (1980), UC Berkeley; later attended Stanford’s executive program.
strings.highlights.h1.title: From chip design to the flash industry
strings.highlights.h1.text: After engineering roles, he helped establish SanDisk and develop nonvolatile-memory designs, systems and products for large-scale use.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Leading a capital-intensive memory business
strings.highlights.h2.text: At Micron he combines engineering, products and global manufacturing through supply cycles and customer changes; research, manufacturing and management teams share the achievements.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discussing AI memory demand and investment
strings.timeline.t1.text: In the fiscal 2026 results release, he emphasized technology, product and manufacturing investment as chairman/CEO and offered expectations for the following year.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Becoming Micron chairman
strings.timeline.t2.text: After the annual meeting he succeeded Bob Switz, working alongside lead independent director Lynn Dugle in the board’s leadership structure.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becoming Micron CEO
strings.timeline.t3.text: He joined as president, CEO and director, bringing long experience at a flash company to another memory manufacturer.
strings.timeline.t4.title: SanDisk sold to Western Digital
strings.timeline.t4.text: The acquisition ended his SanDisk president/CEO tenure; he then briefly served on Western Digital’s board to support integration.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becoming SanDisk president and CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: He assumed top operational leadership and continued development of flash products and systems.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Co-founding SanDisk
strings.timeline.t6.text: With Eli Harari, Jack Yuan and fellow founders, he established a company exploring flash-based solid-state storage.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Master’s degree and chip-design work
strings.timeline.t7.text: After his Berkeley EECS master’s, he designed EPROMs at Intel and later held engineering roles at other semiconductor companies.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing Berkeley undergraduate studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: His EECS bachelor’s degree provided foundations for a career in memory circuits and systems.
